items.question: What is Document Doctor?
items.answer: Document Doctor is one web app with the document and file tools people need at work: a translator, summarizer and extractor for documents, a PDF ⇄ Word converter, PDF merge & split, and an image resizer and compressor.

items.question: Do I need to install anything or create an account?
items.answer: No. Every tool runs in your browser. Open the tool, upload your file, and download the result.

items.question: Which file types and sizes are supported?
items.answer: The translator, summarizer and extractor accept PDF and Word (.docx) files up to 5 MB. The converter and PDF tools accept files up to 10 MB, and you can merge up to 20 PDFs at once. The image tools accept JPG, PNG and WEBP up to 10 MB.

items.question: What happens to my files?
items.answer: The summarizer, extractor, converter, PDF and image tools process your file and return the result without keeping a copy. The translator saves your translated document so you can reopen it in the editor and download it again.

items.question: Can I check or edit what the AI produces?
items.answer: Yes. Translations open in a browser editor where you can change text, headings, lists, links and tables before you export. Extracted details are marked as AI-found, so you can check important ones against the document.

items.question: Which languages are supported?
items.answer: Indonesian, English, Chinese, Japanese, Korean, French, German and Spanish. You can translate from any of these into any other, and get summaries in any of them.

items.question: Can I use scanned PDFs?
items.answer: Not yet for the AI tools. The translator, summarizer and extractor need PDFs with selectable text. Scanned PDFs can still be merged, split, or converted — they come out as images in Word.
